automations.name: Lead intake and scoring
automations.what: Scores each form lead from budget, company size, timeline and email type, logs it to a sheet and emails the owner about hot leads.
automations.evidence: Scoring rules are covered by tests, including a check that the helper matches the n8n node on 180 inputs.
automations.next: Rebuilt as a Wrenbook copy at the cutover.

automations.name: Demo booking agent
automations.what: Offers real free slots by email and books the one a person picks. The model can only choose from slots that code already checked.
automations.evidence: Booking Core and the three tools work on a fixture calendar. The 40-email evaluation has not been run.
automations.next: Gmail trigger and drafts, a Google Calendar connection, then the evaluation. There is no public demo yet.

automations.name: Support inbox triage
automations.what: Classifies, prioritises and labels support email, flags anything a person must handle, and saves a reply as a Gmail draft that is never sent.
automations.evidence: On 54 labelled emails (a development set): 98.1% category accuracy, 100% needs-human recall, 5 of 5 injection attempts flagged, 0 unsafe drafts.
automations.next: A clean full re-run of the evaluation is still owed.

automations.name: Voice line
automations.what: A hands-free voice assistant that answers from the knowledge base and points callers who want a demo to the sales form.
automations.evidence: 15 test questions run as text on 2026-11-11: 15 of 15 right on facts and refusals in the third run, after two prompt changes made while looking at those same questions. Speech and the voice are untested, and 3 answers are longer than the 1 to 3 sentences a call needs.
automations.next: Shorten long answers, test with a real microphone, deploy as its own site and decide whether to turn off login protection.

automations.name: Invoice extraction
automations.what: Reads a bill image, extracts vendor, dates, currency and amounts, and approves it only when the amounts add up and confidence is high. Everything else is marked Needs review.
automations.evidence: On 12 invented sample bills (one run): the 4 flawed bills were all sent to Needs review and 7 of 8 readable bills were approved with every field right. 1 bill, a heavily blurred one, was approved with wrong values because its amounts added up and the model sounded sure.
automations.next: Add a date-plausibility check and test it on new bills, add a Needs-review alert, and run again on real phone photos.
